_doc: Release Manifest precursor. Describes WHAT is being released so the gate checks a committed declaration rather than whatever flags an operator typed. commitSha/buildId/deploymentId are left null until a release is cut - the gate fills the comparison from the build itself, and only enforces a field that is set here. This is NOT the Change Registry: no change IDs, no Firestore, no UI.

_changeNotes.MOD-0024: Cost-centre selector search and recursive selection. The shared selector used by the classic Dashboard and the Custom Dashboard Builder gains a search box matching code, Arabic name and English name where present - case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant, and folding Arabic spelling variants through the existing normaliseLookupText rather than a new normaliser. Results keep hierarchy context: a matched child is shown under its ancestors and a matched parent with its branch, never as a flat list, and search changes only the rows shown, never the selection. Checkboxes are now recursive: checking a node selects it and its entire branch resolved from the FULL hierarchy (so a search cannot narrow what a tick selects), unchecking removes that branch and un-ticks its ancestors without touching any other branch, a partly selected branch shows its parents as indeterminate, and a parent becomes checked once all its children are. Select All adds every classified root, or every match while searching. All descendants, ancestors and children come from the shared hierarchy resolver over the already-loaded hierarchy; selection is local state with ids as identity, typing and ticking issue no Firestore read or write. The production and financial scopes read a materialised branch exactly as they read the parent alone, so Dashboard, Builder and Reports totals are unchanged for the same selection. No Firestore rule, schema, Report, AI, Production Records or production data changed
_changeNotes.DB-0023: Dashboard cost-centre unification and financial values. The classic Dashboard and the Custom Dashboard Builder each offered a flat legacy press/furnace list as the organisational filter; both now use ONE shared hierarchical cost-centre selector grouped under the existing 5/6/7/8/9 classifications, with multi-select checkboxes where a parent includes every descendant and a leaf is itself the target. What a selection covers is decided only by the shared resolver: for quantity it resolves node -> descendants -> linked equipment and is passed into the same filterUniversalRecords Reports uses, so Dashboard, Builder widgets, the Builder print view and its Excel export keep exactly the records Reports keeps for the same scope. An audit found no financial transaction storage anywhere, so the minimum model was added: a financialTransactions collection (date, accountCode, costCenterCode, amount, optional description/reference, importBatchId) with a dedicated Master Data importer beside Financial Accounts that never routes through Historical Import, validates the account and cost centre by exact code, and imports valid rows while keeping invalid rows on screen with their reason; writes go through the audited createMasterDataItem. The Dashboard gains a Metric Type selector (Quantities / Financial values): money is summed only from actual transactions, shown in its own card, never added to tonnage, and filtered only by date and cost centre - product, customer, shift and stage do not apply to it; transactions are read only when financial values are shown. Firestore rules gain a purely additive financialTransactions block (read signed-in, write admin, the financialAccounts pattern); it must be deployed separately before transactions can be read or imported. The reconciliation utility is kept because unresolved conflicts remain. No production record, legacy data, permission or Master Data category changed
_changeNotes.UI-0022: Master Data unification. The screen carried THREE category controls at once - a dropdown, a multi-select panel and a category row - and the dropdown opened the hierarchy maintenance modal when cost centres were chosen, so browsing cost-centre master data was not reachable at all. Two of the three are removed; one row is the whole navigation. Presses, furnaces, mills and the legacy departments list are no longer primary categories: they are the same business entities the imported hierarchy already represents, and listing them again showed one machine as two master records. Their collections are untouched and still reached through the equipment -> hierarchyNodeId link that Production Records, Reports and the assistant use. Cost Centers now serve the imported hierarchy itself, registered as a normal tab so the SAME cache-first read and live subscription serve it, with the 5/6/7/8/9 classifications inline on the same screen and never in a modal. The generic column-mapped importer is excluded from the hierarchy at the type level, since it has its own Sheet1 importer. No data deleted, no production record touched, no Firestore rule, schema or permission changed
_changeNotes.UI-0021: Master Data three-panel organisation. Area 1 is a multi-select code-type picker with checkboxes over the seven registry categories; Area 2 shows exactly the selected ones and switches which is active; Area 3 shows only the active category's data, with an explicit empty state instead of a stale table. Unticking the active category moves focus rather than leaving Area 3 pointing at something no longer listed, and a category that is not selected can never become active. Cost Centres gain 5/6/7/8/9 sub-category filtering that REUSES the existing Sheet1 root-category rule (ROOT_CATEGORY_CODES/ROOT_CATEGORY_LABELS, root = the code's first character) rather than restating it - a code like 0501 is therefore reported as unclassified rather than forced into 5, since the leading zero is significant. The sub-filter is one more AND over the existing search, status and prefix filters. activeTab remains the engine, so the table, Add/Edit modal, importers, export, per-row actions, permissions and audit are untouched; the Cost Center Hierarchy browser and the reconciliation utility stay separate utilities, not categories
_changeNotes.MOD-0020: Enable Apply Safe Matches. The panel action, disabled in 3.15.1 while the UI was being verified, now writes the validated plan through the applier service that has been in place and tested since 3.15.0. The button applies exactly `plannedLinks` - the plan the panel is displaying - so the confirmed count is the written count, and nothing is re-matched at write time: conflicts and no-counterpart rows never enter the plan, so they cannot be written. One field, hierarchyNodeId, on one legacy equipment record, through the audited updateMasterDataItem. Failures isolate with no rollback; a row already pointing at the planned node is skipped, so a second run writes nothing. After a successful apply the equipment list is re-read with skipCache so the panel recomputes and the applied rows stop showing as pending. No production document, Firestore rule, schema, permission, Report or AI code changed
_changeNotes.FIX-0019: Make the reconciliation reachable. The panel shipped in 3.14/3.15 was an inline banner gated on being on an equipment tab AND having a non-zero matched or ambiguous count, so with the hierarchy not yet imported both counts were zero and it rendered on no tab at all - the feature existed in the bundle and nowhere on screen. It is now a dedicated Master Data utility, "Reconcile Codes with Hierarchy", beside the existing quality-report actions, opening a panel that always shows all four buckets including zeroes and an explicit no-data state. Reconciliation now spans presses, furnaces and mills together instead of only the open tab. Read-only by design for this step: the applier service is not imported by the screen at all and the Apply button is rendered disabled, so opening the panel cannot write. The Cost Center Hierarchy browser is a separate control and is untouched
_changeNotes.MOD-0018: Persist the safe legacy-to-hierarchy links. A new CONFLICT outcome was added first, because the 3.14.0 plan would have overwritten a record already linked to a DIFFERENT node - harmless while nothing was written, a silent reassignment once it is. Conflicts now never reach `matched`, so they cannot reach the plan: the protection is structural rather than a filter. The applier consumes the already-validated plan without re-matching, writes one field on one legacy record through the existing audited updateMasterDataItem (permissions, validation, audit and cache invalidation inherited), isolates every failure so 97 successes survive 3 errors with no rollback, and skips a row already pointing at the planned node so a second run writes nothing. Master Data gains an Apply Safe Matches action with an explicit confirmation naming the exact count and stating that historical records are untouched. Ambiguous, conflicting and unmatched rows stay visible for manual review. No production document, Firestore rule, schema or permission changed
_changeNotes.MOD-0017: Legacy code reconciliation and true multi-select hierarchy. A new pure engine matches legacy equipment records to imported hierarchy nodes by exact business code WITHIN the same category, returning MATCHED / AMBIGUOUS / UNMATCHED; names are carried into the report but never compared, so differing names for the same code reconcile and a shared code across categories never does. Only an unambiguous one-to-one match is safe to persist, and the release writes nothing - Master Data shows the dry run. The derived link also completes equipment links in memory so a hierarchy leaf resolves to its legacy equipment immediately, which is what ends the false "no equipment" on a childless node: having no children is no longer treated as having no equipment. The selector became multi-select at EVERY level - each level is the deduplicated union of the children of what is ticked above it, a deeper tick narrows (so parent plus child cannot double-count), unticking a parent cascades its descendants away, and select-all covers only the nodes visible at that level. Reports, AI and the Dashboard inherit the corrected links through the one shared resolver
_changeNotes.MOD-0016: Hierarchical production filter UI. Production Records gains a multi-level production-centre drill-down: level 1 is the hierarchy's real roots, each later level is exactly the chosen node's children, depth is whatever the data has, and equipment is ticked with checkboxes at the current branch. Stopping at any level means the whole branch below it; ticking narrows to exactly what is ticked and can never widen. Navigation discards deeper levels and ticks from the branch being left, so a stale selection cannot leak across branches. The Dashboard equipment selector now follows the selected stage instead of always listing presses - options come from a registry declaration of which equipment each stage actually records, read off the entry forms: only pressing writes pressId/furnaceId, so every other stage now says it has no equipment rather than offering a filter that could only ever match nothing; an incompatible selection is cleared when the stage changes. Both screens resolve through the one shared resolver and agree on the same equipment ids. filterUniversalRecords gained an additive furnaceId clause that Reports never set
_changeNotes.AI-0015: AI hierarchy integration. A new deterministic lookup service (hierarchyNodeLookupPure) resolves production-centre text to a hierarchy node by exact code, then exact canonical name, then exact localized name, returning FOUND / AMBIGUOUS / NOT_FOUND. Ambiguous names ask which branch was meant using real paths; unknown names say so rather than answering zero; fuzzy matching is offered only as a did-you-mean suggestion and never resolves. The EXISTING generateReport tool gained one optional productionCenters field and routes the resolved node ids through the same shared equipment resolver and the same filterUniversalRecords the Reports screen uses, so assistant totals equal report totals by construction rather than by coincidence. No provider, no Global AI Chat, no aggregation formula, no permission, no Firestore rule and no production record changed; the legacy productionQueryTools path is deliberately left out because it aggregates differently
_changeNotes.UI-0014: Hierarchy-aware reporting. The Reports screen gains a production-centre scope selector: choosing a node scopes the report to that node plus every descendant node's linked equipment, resolved once through the shared resolver and deduplicated before any record is examined, so overlapping branches never double-count. A stage record's equipment is read from rawData (pressId/furnaceId/machineId/equipmentId), ALL of them rather than the first, so a record naming both a press and a furnace belongs to both branches yet is still counted once. The scope is an additional AND beside date, stage, product, customer, employee and shift; with no selection the filtering is the identity case and every report is byte-identical to before. Aggregation formulas, exports and permissions are untouched - export already flows from the same filtered dataset. Records from the seven stages that carry no equipment reference are excluded from a press/furnace scope rather than silently kept, because membership must be provable. No AI, Firestore rule, schema or production document changed
_changeNotes.MOD-0013: Equipment -> hierarchy link. Press, Furnace and Mill master records gain a persisted, nullable hierarchyNodeId holding a stable hierarchy node id. A production record is now resolved to the hierarchy as record -> pressId/furnaceId -> equipment master record -> hierarchyNodeId -> ancestors, so selecting a parent node includes every descendant node's linked equipment WITHOUT modifying a single historical production document and with no migration. The shared hierarchy resolver gained the equipment layer (buildEquipmentByNode, resolveEquipmentForHierarchyNode(s), validateEquipmentLink); there is still exactly one descendant walk. Master Data gains a node selector on the equipment tabs, a link-status column and an unlinked-count banner. Assignment is explicit: no fuzzy matching is used as the authoritative relationship. Financial Accounts and Cost Centers remain Master-Data-only. No Firestore rule changed - presses/furnaces already allowed admin writes
_changeNotes.UI-0012: Production Records code filter: the press-only selector is replaced by a category then code filter driven by the shared Master Data registry. Adds furnace, customer and shift as filter dimensions and multi-code selection, with an empty code list meaning ALL so that mode never materialises the code list. The registry gained a separate legacyProductionFields declaration because the `production` collection is a different record shape from UniversalStageRecord - it has no stageType but does carry pressId, furnaceId and shiftId. Financial Accounts and Cost Centers remain Master-Data-only: no production record field links to them. The hierarchy expansion is shared with the stage-record resolver but no legacy category is hierarchical, because nothing links a production record to a hierarchy node
_changeNotes.MOD-0011: Row-selection foundation for the Production Records table: per-row and header checkboxes in a dedicated column, a visible/selected counter, select-all-visible and deselect-all controls, and pruning of stale selections on filter change. Reuses the existing bulkEditPure selection primitives rather than adding a second selection architecture. Selection is UI state only - no Firestore read or write - and no bulk action of any kind is attached to it; in particular no bulk delete
_changeNotes.UI-0010: Financial Accounts import opens a dedicated Master Data importer instead of the Historical Excel Import screen: the action no longer navigates to the bulk-entry route (which App.tsx renders as DataImportView); a new in-place modal reuses the existing financialAccounts schema, XLSX reader, row validation, duplicate detection and chunked commit, adds sheet selection and parent/cycle relationship checks, and keeps partial import so invalid rows never block valid ones
_changeNotes.DB-0009: Category-first Master Data over an extensible registry; Financial Accounts master data with Excel import and hierarchical editing (new financialAccounts collection and its Firestore rule); one shared generic hierarchy resolver reused by Master Data, Production Review and production aggregation; hierarchical cost-centre editing with cycle, self-parent and unknown-parent protection
